purpose: Privileged setup wrapper. Sets up cgroups, chroot, network namespace, resource limits, drops privileges, and exec()s the statically-linked Firecracker binary.

flags.name: --id
flags.doc: Required. Unique microVM identifier. Alphanumeric+hyphen, max 64 chars.

flags.name: --exec-file
flags.doc: Required. Path to the Firecracker binary (statically linked, same version as jailer).

flags.name: --uid
flags.doc: Required. Non-privileged uid to drop to.

flags.name: --gid
flags.doc: Required. Non-privileged gid to drop to.

flags.name: --cgroup-version
flags.doc: Cgroup hierarchy. Default 1; use 2 on cgroup-v2 hosts.

flags.name: --cgroup
flags.doc: Repeatable. Cgroup setting (e.g., cpuset.cpus=0). Avoids needing root on the orchestrator side.

flags.name: --parent-cgroup
flags.doc: Place microVM cgroup under this parent. Default: <exec_file_name>.

flags.name: --netns
flags.doc: Path to network namespace handle (e.g., /var/run/netns/myvm). Jailer setns()s into it.

flags.name: --new-pid-ns
flags.doc: Spawn Firecracker into a new PID namespace (clone(CLONE_NEWPID)).

flags.name: -- <firecracker args>
flags.doc: End-of-options marker; everything after is forwarded to Firecracker. Note jailer always passes --id.

examples.expected_output: Sandboxed Firecracker w/ 100ms CPU per 100ms quota, 512 MiB memory cap, fresh PID/net namespaces, fd limit 4096, auto-loading config
Daemonized Firecracker; jailer returns immediately; PID stored in <chroot>/firecracker.pid if --new-pid-ns also set

purpose: Create a network namespace for the jailer to attach via --netns. Combine with TAP creation inside the netns to give the microVM an isolated network stack.

examples.invocation: ip netns add myvm; ip netns exec myvm ip tuntap add tap0 mode tap; ip netns exec myvm ip addr add 172.16.0.1/24 dev tap0; ip netns exec myvm ip link set tap0 up

purpose: Pre-create a cgroup hierarchy for the jailer to use (alternative to letting jailer create it inline via --cgroup). Useful when the orchestrator is non-privileged.

examples.scenario: Pre-arming for a non-privileged jailer launch

purpose: Read the host-side PID of the jailed Firecracker process. Recorded by jailer when --new-pid-ns is used (since the jail-internal PID is meaningless to the host).
Communicate with a jailed Firecracker — the API socket lives INSIDE the chroot tree. Orchestrator must use the absolute host path to the socket.
